title: Straight Pipe Under Internal Pressure — Pressure Design Thickness
scope_note: tm = t + c, where pressure design thickness t = (P*D) / [2*(S*E*W + P*Y)] for t < D/6. W is weld strength reduction factor (=1.0 for normal temp); Y is material/temp coefficient from Table 304.1.1-1 (0.4 for ferritic steels <= 900°F); c is mechanical + corrosion allowance (FCA).

title: Pressure Design Thickness for In-Service Piping
scope_note: Specifies Barlow formula t = (P*D) / (2*S*E) for simple in-service wall thickness, and notes equivalence to ASME B31.3 formula t = (P*D) / [2*(S*E*W + P*Y)]. Governs pressure design thickness prior to structural minimum comparison.
source_file: API 574 Inspection Practices for Piping System Components.pdf

title: Structural Minimum Thickness Determination
scope_note: Minimum required thickness cannot be lower than structural minimum thickness (Annex D, Tables D.2a/D.2b) to prevent sag, buckling, and collapse at pipe supports regardless of pressure design result.
source_file: API 574 Inspection Practices for Piping System Components.pdf

title: Required Thickness Determination
scope_note: The required thickness of a pipe shall be the greater of pressure design thickness or structural minimum thickness. Refers to API 574 Section 10 for pressure design and structural minimum formulas.

title: Long-Term (LT) Corrosion Rate Determination
scope_note: Corrosion rate (LT) = (t_initial - t_actual) / time (years) between t_initial and t_actual. Point-to-point method calculated for each individual CML.

title: Short-Term (ST) Corrosion Rate Determination
scope_note: Corrosion rate (ST) = (t_previous - t_actual) / time (years) between t_previous and t_actual. Reflects recent interval degradation rate.

title: Governing Corrosion Rate Comparison and Selection
scope_note: LT and ST corrosion rates should be compared to see which results in the shortest remaining life as part of data assessment. The authorized inspector selects the governing rate best reflecting the process.

title: Remaining Life Calculations
scope_note: Remaining life (years) = (t_actual - t_required) / corrosion rate [inches (mm) per year]. t_required is computed by design formulas (pressure and structural) before corrosion allowance.

title: Inspection Intervals Without RBI — Half Remaining Life Rule
scope_note: For Class 1, 2, and 3 piping, thickness measurement intervals shall not exceed one-half the remaining life, or Table 1 maximums, whichever is less. When remaining life < 4 years, interval may be full remaining life up to maximum 2 years.

title: Recommended Maximum Thickness Measurement Intervals by Piping Class
scope_note: Class 1: 5 years max. Class 2: 10 years max. Class 3: 10 years max. Class 4: optional. Injection points: 3 years max.

title: Piping Service Classification (Class 1 through Class 4)
scope_note: Class 1: Highest emergency consequence (autorefrigeration, rapid vaporization, H2S > 3%, HF acid, over water). Class 2: Unit process piping (on-site hydrocarbons below boiling point, hydrogen, acids). Class 3: Low volatility, off-site/storage, below flash point. Class 4: Utilities (steam, air, nitrogen, water).

title: Magnetic Particle Examination (MT) — Acceptance Criteria
scope_note: Only indications with any dimension > 1.5 mm (1/16 in.) are relevant. Linear indication: length > 3*width. Rounded indication: circular or elliptical with length <= 3*width. All surfaces shall be free of: (1) relevant linear indications, (2) relevant rounded indications > 5.0 mm (> 3/16 in.), (3) 4 or more relevant rounded indications in a line separated by 1.5 mm or less edge-to-edge.

title: Liquid Penetrant Examination (PT) — Acceptance Criteria
scope_note: Only indications with any dimension > 1.5 mm (1/16 in.) are relevant. Linear indication: length > 3*width. Rounded indication: circular or elliptical with length <= 3*width. All surfaces shall be free of: (1) relevant linear indications, (2) relevant rounded indications > 5.0 mm (> 3/16 in.), (3) 4 or more relevant rounded indications in a line separated by 1.5 mm or less edge-to-edge.
